messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted for surgical treatment of cecal cancer with sclerosing mesenteritis. The surgery involved a right colectomy with excision of a diffusely thick mesenterium with multiple yellowish nodules. Pathology report revealed Astler-Coller C2 cecal adenocarcinoma and diffuse sclerosing mesenteritis of the excised mesenterium. The patient followed oncologic treatment consisting in capecidabine under close surveillance of his coagulation parameters with no reported abdominal pain or discomfort. A CT scan was performed 6 months later in the context of cancer follow-up, which did not demonstrate any significant radiological changes of the sclerosing mesenteritis.

History and Physical:
An 83-year-old male was admitted with a past medical history of atrial fibrillation, coronary heart disease, and previous surgeries including an appendicectomy in his childhood and a laparoscopic cholecystectomy three years ago. He presented with symptoms of weight loss, abdominal discomfort, and persistent fatigue leading to a complete laboratory examination demonstrating iron deficiency anemia.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Plan:
The patient underwent a right hemicolectomy. Oncologic treatment with capecidabine was initiated post-surgery, and the patient was discharged with close follow-up appointments. 

Disposition:
The patient was discharged in a stable condition.

Follow-up:
The patient is advised to follow up with his oncologist for continued cancer surveillance.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
Admission was for surgical treatment of a cecal adenocarcinoma, a malignant neoplasm of the colon. That places it in chapter C. Malignant neoplasm of the colon (caecum) is category C18.

CODE: C18
